inputs: data/machine_geometry.json (R01 shared geometry: stator, winding, R_coil, rotor_wrsm layout; WRSM gap not yet set)
02_analytics/hesm_envelope.py (T03c WRSM s=0 / HESM s=0.25 models, T03 stator, N=16)
board/prior_work.md P1 (rectifier 99/87 %), P3 decks (harvesting coil, superimposed voltage)

assumptions.g_eff_note: T03 k_c k_sat = 1.3 mm; R01 WRSM gap open -> sensitivity 1.08/2/3 mm
assumptions.rotor_tank: series-tuned at f_r0; rotor leakage cancelled; rectifier = resistive load
assumptions.voltage_budget: peak sum: V_fund + V_inj <= V_max (rms of sinusoids, conservative)
assumptions.current_budget: start: peak sum (conservative) and rms sum reported
not_included: saturation-dependent incremental permeability for the nu-wave
PWM sidebands of the injected wave
rotor eddy loss in solid parts (laminated rotor assumed)

injection_choice.f_stator_rule: f_i = |f_r0 - nu f_m| (0 Hz at 90 km/h)
injection_choice.zero_sequence: not possible: an isolated-neutral module carries no zero-sequence current (orders divisible by 3 put a module's coils in phase); the SPB-specific freedom is an independent space order per module pattern, not a zero-sequence path

torque_ripple_and_forces.average_torque_with_field: none: nu = 8 is not in the rotor-field spectrum and the wave is asynchronous (f_r0 != 0)

crosstalk.remedy: tune the two tanks to different rotor frequencies f_r1 != f_r2; the inactive tank is off-resonance

bipolar_for_pole_changing.topology: P1 dual-input/dual-output with the two WPT transmitters replaced by two injected space orders (or two tank frequencies on one order): channel 1 rectifier -> group B (+), channel 2 rectifier -> group B (-) anti-parallel, P1 self-driven blocking switches; group A from a third tank (frequency-selected). Polarity = which pattern the SPB injects.

injection.rotor_hardware: harvest winding (order 8, polyphase) + tank capacitors + diode rectifier (+ P1 blocking switches for bipolar)

brushes.note: 2 V brush drop at an assumed 20 A / 200 V field + H-bridge 98 %; wear and maintenance
